correctness.rationale: For every Fourier difference in the full square box, integration along a primitive closed geodesic is zero unless the difference is a multiple of its primitive normal. A nonzero vector is normal to only one unoriented direction; hence exactness decouples. The normalized Toeplitz moment matrix is the identity and factors through one column per loop, proving the sharp component count and regular-polygon equality case. Multiplying this count by the primitive-geodesic length gives the sharp per-direction and global length bounds. The standalone checker validates finite examples but is not treated as an infinite proof. For J=2 both coordinate directions attain their separate bounds; J>=3 forces a strict summed length bound, because there are only two coordinate direction classes.

value.rationale: The motivation is optimal trajectory acquisition for periodic bandlimited fields when multiple independent moving sensors, directions and sensor weights are permitted. The result completely resolves a natural optimization class beyond the parallel equal-weight case and shows a structural no-cooperation theorem: every distinct direction incurs the full baseline arclength. The exact rigidity and unique optimizer guide whether mixing line directions can reduce exact-Parseval travel. This is more than a small numerical gain or a renamed one-direction computation.
